questions.text:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var s []int
	fmt.Println(len(s))
	fmt.Println(cap(s))
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	s := make([]int, 3)
	fmt.Println(len(s))
	fmt.Println(cap(s))
	fmt.Println(s[2])
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	s := make([]int, 2, 5)
	fmt.Println(len(s))
	fmt.Println(cap(s))
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	s := make([]int, 2, 4)
	s[0], s[1] = 1, 2
	t := s[:3]
	fmt.Println(len(t))
	fmt.Println(cap(t))
	fmt.Println(t[2])
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var s []int
	s = append(s, 4)
	fmt.Println(len(s))
	fmt.Println(s[0])
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	s := make([]int, 2, 4)
	s[0], s[1] = 1, 2
	t := s
	s = append(s, 9)
	fmt.Println(len(t))
	fmt.Println(len(s))
	u := t[:3]
	fmt.Println(u[2])
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	s := make([]int, 2)
	s[0], s[1] = 1, 2
	t := s
	s = append(s, 3)
	s[0] = 7
	fmt.Println(t[0])
	fmt.Println(s[0])
	fmt.Println(len(t))
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	s := make([]int, 1, 3)
	s[0] = 5
	t := append(s, 6)
	s[0] = 8
	fmt.Println(s[0])
	fmt.Println(t[0])
	fmt.Println(len(s))
	fmt.Println(len(t))
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	s := make([]int, 4, 6)
	fmt.Println(s[3])
	fmt.Println(len(s))
	fmt.Println(cap(s))
}
What three fields make up a slice header?
options: A pointer to an array, length, and capacity
Only length and capacity
The elements themselves and a length
A pointer and a hash of the elements

questions.text: Where do a slice’s elements live?
options: Inside the header, next to len and cap
In a backing array. The header holds a pointer to it
In a separate table per index
Only on the call stack, with no array

questions.text: When do two slices see a write to the same element?
options: Always. Every slice in the process shares one array
Only if they came from copy
When their windows overlap on the same backing array
Never. A write copies the array at once

questions.text: When does append allocate a new backing array?
options: On every call
Only if the slice was nil
Only if the length is already zero
When the new length is greater than the current capacity

questions.text: How does a nil slice differ from []int{}?
options: Both have len and cap 0, but only nil compares equal to nil
[]int{} has length 1
You cannot pass nil to len
They have different zero values for elements

questions.text: What does make([]int, n) put in the new elements?
options: Random numbers
Zeros, the type’s zero value
Nothing: indexes below n are unusable until append
A copy of n from another slice

questions.text: How many elements does copy transfer, and what happens to len(dst)?
options: Always len(src); len(dst) becomes that number
Always len(dst); leftover src elements are appended
min(len(dst), len(src)); dst length does not grow
cap(dst); the unused tail of dst is trimmed

questions.text: What are len and cap of t := s[i:j]?
options: len = j, cap = i
len = j - i, cap = len(s)
len = i, cap = j - i
len = j - i, cap = cap(s) - i

questions.text: How far can you extend a slice with s[:k] without a panic?
options: k may be up to cap(s) inclusive
k cannot be greater than len(s)
k may be any positive number
k must be strictly less than len(s)

questions.text: What happens to the old variable if you ignore append’s return value?
options: Its len still grows in place
The header in that variable does not change: len stays the same
The variable becomes nil
It is a compile error

questions.text: What happens to an array if you write an element through a slice taken as a[:]?
options: The array does not change: the slice copies every element at once
Only a heap copy changes; the stack array stays the same
The array element changes: the slice looks at that same array
The array becomes a slice and loses its fixed length

questions.text: What does a function receive when you pass it a slice?
options: A pointer to the header, with no copy
A full copy of the backing array
A copy of the length only, with no pointer
A copy of the header. The array behind the pointer is the same until append allocates a new one

questions.text: A var s []int has both length and capacity 0.
The expression []int{} == nil is true.
make([]int, 3) has capacity 3.
append always allocates a new backing array.
copy grows len(dst) when src is longer than dst.
Two slices that share an array and overlap see each other’s element writes.
For any slice s with len(s) >= 1, cap(s[1:]) == cap(s)-1.
For a non-empty slice, s[len(s)] is valid and yields the last element.
make([]int, 2, 8) has length 2.
Passing a slice to a function copies the header, not the whole array.
Calling append(s, x) without using the result still increases that variable’s len.
A slice header stores the elements themselves inside its three fields, with no array.
What three fields does a slice header have?
questions.answer: A pointer to the backing array, length, and capacity.

questions.text: What are len and cap of make([]int, 2, 5)?
What are len and cap of var s []int?
questions.answer: Both are 0. It is a nil slice.

questions.text: How many elements does copy(dst, src) transfer?
questions.answer: min(len(dst), len(src)). dst length does not grow.

questions.text: When can append keep the same backing array?
questions.answer: When the new length is not greater than the current capacity.

questions.text: What are the elements of make([]int, n) before any write?
What is the length of s[i:j]?
What is the capacity of s[i:j]?
Is []int{} equal to nil?
questions.answer: No. Both have length 0, but the empty literal does not compare equal to nil.

questions.text: What must you do with append’s result?
questions.answer: Assign it: it returns a (possibly new) slice header.

questions.text: What happens to an array when you write through a slice taken as a[:]?
questions.answer: The array’s own element changes: the slice looks at that array.

questions.text: What is copied when you pass a slice to a function?
questions.answer: Only the header. The backing array is the same until append allocates a new one.
